submission.justification: Module-D1 has the highest light yield (38 PE/MeV at 20% coverage) but fails thermal cycling at 30% (20 cycles, 300K-87K), well above the 5% robustness limit; its thin light-guide bonding cracks on cooldown, and modules cannot be replaced after the cryostat is filled. Module-D2 fails only 2% and is the best robust option (27 PE/MeV at 20%). Light collection rises roughly as coverage^0.8, so at the 30% maximum (within the 30 feedthrough limit confirmed in the meeting notes) D2 should reach about 37 PE/MeV. This is an extrapolation from the 2025 simulation, not a fresh simulation run at 30%. Module-D3 is also robust (0.5%) but gives only about 18 PE/MeV at 20%, so it is dominated by D2.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three candidate designs
requirements.evidence: Module-D2 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Robust for inaccessible post-fill operation (<=5% failures after 20 thermal cycles)

requirements.evidence: Recommended coverage is 30%, the upper bound; feedthroughs suffice for 30% per meeting notes 2026-01-20.

Among robust designs D2 has the highest yield (27 PE/MeV at 20%, 2025 simulation), extrapolating to about 37 PE/MeV at 30% using coverage^0.8. The 30% value is an extrapolation, not a direct simulation. D1 (38 PE/MeV at 20%) is higher but fails robustness.
